title: map
description: A map of regions from a GeoJSON file, with layers of data over them: a choropleth that colours each region by a value from a CSV, a raster (a picture over the land: a value ramp, classes or a mask) or points (places sized and coloured by a column), in the theme's palettes, with a hatch for a region or land that has no value and a dot for a region too small to see. Steps bring layers in and out (each adds its legend row), highlight regions and put names on the map, fly the map and an inset to a region, and play a time-lapse raster through its frames with a corner panel of the frame's label and numbers. With `compact` the same map draws small, as a second view, with one optional `caption`.

boundaries.description: Path to a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of Polygon and MultiPolygon features, relative to the deck root: the regions, drawn as land in the surface colour with borders in the rule colour. Files written by `sf` or `geopandas` (counter-clockwise, RFC 7946) work as they are. Fixed for the element: a change on a step redraws the map at once.

id.description: The feature property that identifies a region (compared as text), which `highlight`, `labels` and a layer's `key` column refer to. Without it, each feature's own `id`.

name.description: The feature property whose text `labels` show. Without it (or for a feature without that property), a label shows the region's id.

projection.description: The map projection, centred on the regions and fitted to the element with a margin. "conic-equal-area" (the default) keeps areas true and, for a country or a region of one, nearly its shape (its two parallels sit a sixth of the way in from each end of the regions' latitudes). A world or continent map names "equal-earth", which keeps areas but narrows shapes near the equator; "mercator" keeps shapes but enlarges areas away from the equator.

areas.description: Path to a CSV with one row per region, relative to the deck root: a choropleth. A layer has exactly one of `areas`, `raster` and `points`.

raster.description: Path to a raster file, relative to the deck root: a JSON that gives `bounds`, what the grey levels mean in `value` and a greyscale PNG in `src`, or, for a time-lapse, a list of labelled PNGs in `frames` (see `frame`). A value raster takes the scale props (`classes`, `midpoint`, `domain`), a raster of classes the categorical palette in order, and a raster of one class (a mask) the layer's `color`. Land the raster has no data for is hatched, and the legend adds a "no data" row. Clipped to the land outline unless `clip` is false.

points.description: Path to a CSV with one row per place, relative to the deck root: circles at the `lon` and `lat` of each row, over the borders. A layer has exactly one of `areas`, `raster` and `points`.

lon.description: For `points`: the column of longitudes, in degrees. A row whose longitude is empty or not a number is an element error.

lat.description: For `points`: the column of latitudes, in degrees. A row whose latitude is empty or not a number is an element error.

id.description: For `points`: the column that names each point, which `highlight` refers to (compared as text). Without it a point has no name and cannot be highlighted.

size.description: For `points`: the column of values that sizes each point, with an area true to the value: radius 18 px × √(value ÷ largest value), so the largest point has a radius of 18 px. The legend adds a size key of two circles: the largest value rounded down to two significant figures, and the round number (1, 2 or 5 × 10ⁿ) at most a quarter of it (70 gives 70 and 10). Without it every point has a radius of 6 px. A row whose size is empty, not a number or negative is an element error.

key.description: The column that names each row's region, compared as text with the map's `id` ("07" is not 7: declare it in `types`). Default: the map's `id`. A key that matches no region, or a region in two rows, is an element error.

value.description: For `areas`: the column of values that colours each region. An empty cell, or a region without a row, is hatched and adds a "no data" row to the legend: never a colour of the scale.

label.description: The title of the layer's legend row.

types.description: CSV column types, passed to the data loader. Declare a key column of codes with leading zeros as "string".

classes.description: For `areas` and value rasters: class breaks, in increasing order: n breaks make n + 1 classes, coloured in even steps along the sequential palette and labelled `< 5`, `5–10`, …, `≥ 20` in the legend. A value equal to a break is in the class above it.

midpoint.description: For `areas` and value rasters: a value that splits the diverging palette: below it one hue, above it the other. With `classes` it must be one of the breaks.

domain.description: For `areas` and value rasters: the ends of a continuous ramp (no `classes`), used as given; a value past an end takes the end colour. Default: the values' extent (a raster's `min` and `max`), made symmetric about `midpoint` when there is one.

clip.description: For `raster`: whether the picture is clipped to the land outline (the default). A coarse cell whose centre is on land then stops at the coastline instead of sticking out over the sea, and the hatch of land with no data stops there too. With false every cell is drawn whole, for a raster that covers the sea as well. A change on a step crossfades.

color.description: For a raster of one class (a mask): the theme colour role that paints it, such as `accent` (the default), `alert`, `ink` or `muted`. For `points`: the name of a column, if the CSV has one of that name (each distinct value takes a colour of the categorical palette, in order of first appearance, with a swatch each in the legend), else a theme colour role, as for a mask (default `accent`). A name that is neither is an element error.

layers.description: The layers of data, keyed by an id that `shown` refers to. A layer with `areas` is a choropleth: its `value` column colours the regions its `key` column names, through a scale of the theme's palettes (`classes` for stepped classes, `midpoint` for a diverging one, `domain` to fix a ramp's ends), with `label` as the title of its legend row. A layer with `raster` is a picture over the land, drawn between the areas and the borders, with the same scale props. A layer with `points` puts a circle at each row's `lon` and `lat`, over the borders, sized by a `size` column and coloured by a `color` column or role. An object, not a list, so a step can change one layer. A change to a shown layer's data or scale crossfades its colours.

shown.description: The layers on screen, by id, painted in the order `layers` declares them. Default: none (the regions alone). A layer that appears fades in with its legend row; one that leaves fades out. An id `layers` does not have is an element error.

highlight.description: Regions and points to emphasize, by id: they are outlined in ink, and every other region of an areas layer and every other point turns the theme's dim colour (a hatched region stays hatched). A point is named by the `id` column of its layer. Usually set with `only` so it lasts one step. An id that is neither a region nor a point is an element error.

view.description: Where the map looks: a region id or a list of them, fitted with the same margin as the whole map; `{ "bounds": [west, south, east, north] }` in degrees; or null (the default) for the whole map. A view names regions only: an id that is not a region, a point's included, is an element error. A change on a forward step flies the map there over twice the step's duration, zooming out and in again as far as the distance asks: vectors are redrawn as it moves and a raster crossfades from its picture at the start to its picture at the end.

Where the inset looks, as `view` does for the map: a region id or a list of them, a box `{ "bounds": [west, south, east, north] }`, or null for the whole map. A change on a forward step flies the inset alone, as `view` flies the map, over twice the step's duration.

at.description: The corner of the element the inset sits in.

scale.description: Whether the inset has a scale bar, a round length in km at its bottom-left.

inset.description: A second, zoomed view of the same shown layers, in a corner of the element: 36% of its width, with its aspect, 3% of its width in from the two edges. It shows what the map would at `inset.view`, with the same layers, colours, highlight and names. A box on the map marks the part it shows, two dashed lines join the box to the inset (none while the inset covers the box), and a scale bar gives a round length in km. The inset fades in and out; a change of `inset.view` flies the inset only, the box following. Null or absent: no inset.

frame.description: The frame of the time-lapse layers on screen, by its label in their raster files (compared as text: 2015 and "2015" are one frame). One value for the whole map, so every time-lapse layer on it must have the same labels. Default: the first frame. A change on a forward step runs through every frame in between, in the files' order (backward when the new frame comes first), each crossfading into the next at `pace` ms a frame, after everything else the step changes (a flight first, then the run at the end view). The corner panel shows the label of the frame on screen and the `numbers`. A label the files do not have is an element error.

pace.description: How long a run spends on each frame it moves, in ms: a step that moves `frame` on by 18 frames at 700 ms runs for 12.6 s. A step's run, with whatever the step changes before it, may last at most 20 s: split a longer one across steps.

key.description: A key of the frames' `numbers` in a time-lapse raster file. Exactly one time-lapse layer of the map must have it.

label.description: The number's label in the panel, in the deck's language. Without it, the number alone.

format.description: d3-format specifier for the number, localized by the deck language (as `big-number`'s `format`).

numbers.description: The numbers of the frame on screen that the corner panel shows under its label, each after its own label and formatted as declared. During a run each counts linearly from one frame's value to the next. The panel sits at the top-left, or the top-right when the inset is there, while a time-lapse layer is shown. A key no time-lapse layer has, or that two have, is an element error.

labels.description: Regions to name on the map, by id: each label is the region's `name` (else its id) at the centroid of its largest polygon, on a halo of the background colour. Labels that come or go fade. An unknown id is an element error.

legend.description: The corner the legend sits in, its rows stacked away from it: one row per shown layer, with its classes or ramp and, when some region has no value, a hatched "no data" swatch. Default "bottom-left"; false shows no legend.

compact.description: Draw the same map small, as a second view (a locator beside a chart): inside the theme's second-view frame, fitted to the element less the compact pad and the caption's band, with no legend, names, time-lapse panel or inset (`labels`, `legend`, `numbers` and `inset` are ignored). A highlighted region's land takes a tint of the accent, under its ink outline. Layers, `shown`, `view` and `frame` work as at full size.

caption.description: One line of inline Markdown at the label size, in its own band at the top of a compact map (it is drawn only with `compact: true`; it never wraps or shrinks). A change crossfades.
